extra/threat_model_complete.txt.title: map_risks() lookup
note: **Filters the OWASP LLM Top-10 list to risks that apply to this component type.**
- Each risk's applies_to lists the component types it threatens

extra/threat_model_complete.txt.title: score() risk math
note: **Computes likelihood x impact, then bands it LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH.**
- Likelihood comes from component exposure; handling PII raises impact
- LLM02/LLM06 (leakage risks) get an extra impact bump

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Trusted source allowlist
note: **Only chunks from these two PDFs are trusted - provenance filtering.**
- The poisoned document isn't on the list, so it gets dropped

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Filter patterns and thresholds
note: **Three tunables: injection phrases to block, bad output to redact, minimum relevance.**
- Regex lists are a first layer, not a complete defense
- RELEVANCE_MIN drops barely-related chunks attackers rely on

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Chunk filtering gatekeeper
note: **Drops any chunk that's untrusted, matches an injection pattern, or scores low relevance.**
- Each rejection logs a BLOCKED reason - watch for these in the run

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Output redaction pass
note: **Scrubs responses: any BAD_OUTPUT_PATTERNS match becomes [REDACTED].**
- Last line of defense if an injection slips through

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: Jailbreak patterns, topic allowlist
note: **Regexes for common jailbreak phrasing, plus the topics this bot may discuss.**
- Allowlist beats blocklist: anything off-topic is refused by default

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: guard_jailbreak() check
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Rejects input matching any jailbreak regex, reporting which pattern hit.**

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.anchor: if any(t in text.lower() for t in ALLOWED_TOPICS):
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: guard_topic() allowlist check
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Passes input only if it mentions an allowed topic - otherwise refused as off-topic.**

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: guard_length() size cap
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Rejects oversized input - cheap defense against prompt stuffing and abuse.**

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.endAnchor: BANNED_OUTPUT = [r"here is how to make", r"http://", r"\bpassword is\b"]
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: PII and banned-output patterns
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Regexes for SSNs, cards, emails, phones, plus phrases the bot must never emit.**

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: guard_pii() redaction
note: **Replaces each PII match with a [LABEL-REDACTED] tag instead of blocking outright.**
- Returns the fixed text so the user still gets an answer

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: guard_banned() output check
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Blocks responses matching banned patterns (exploit how-tos, raw http:// links, leaked passwords).**

extra/guardrails_complete.txt.title: Wiring guards into pipeline
extra/guardrails_complete.txt.note: **Registers your guards in order: length, jailbreak, topic on input; PII, banned on output.**

extra/secure_agent_complete.txt.title: Least-privilege tool set
note: **The whole control: export_data and delete_records are simply never offered.**
- A hijacked plan calling them is refused before it starts

extra/secure_agent_complete.txt.title: Approval gate logic
note: **Low-risk tools pass; high-risk tools go to an operator, who denies here.**
- In production this would prompt a real human

extra/secure_agent_complete.txt.title: Budget cap check
note: **One comparison: stop the run once MAX_STEPS actions have been attempted.**
- Contains loops and escalation even if every other control fails

extra/secure_server_complete.txt.title: Per-tool scope check
note: **Rejects calls whose token lacks the tools:<name> scope - raises a 403 ToolError.**
- Auth says who you are; this enforces what you may call

extra/observable_agent_complete.txt.title: Span-instrumented tool call
note: **Wraps every tool call in an OTel span with user, tool, sensitive, and status attributes.**
- Denied calls get ERROR status - the anomaly detector reads this
- Prints one [AUDIT] line per request with trace/span ids

extra/observable_agent_complete.txt.title: Anomaly detection rules
note: **Three detectors over captured spans: denied sensitive calls, bursts (3+), sensitive-tool review list.**
- Produces the ANOMALY DETECTION block in the lab output

extra/target_agent_complete.txt.title: Hijack and restricted-intent patterns
note: **Regexes for prompt-hijack phrasing plus intents an HR bot must never act on.**
- Your red-team probes in this lab try to slip past these

extra/target_agent_complete.txt.title: Input screening check
extra/target_agent_complete.txt.note: **Flags input matching any hijack or restricted-intent pattern, naming the rule that hit.**

extra/policy_engine_complete.txt.title: Policy enforcement checks
note: **Runs the YAML policy in order: rate limit, tool deny/allow lists, query types, data scopes.**
- Deny-list wins over allow-list
- Change security_policy.yaml later to alter behavior - no code edits

extra/security_gate_complete.txt.title: Secret detection patterns
extra/security_gate_complete.txt.note: **Regexes for leaked API keys, hardcoded passwords, and AWS keys in source.**

extra/security_gate_complete.txt.title: Secret scan over source
extra/security_gate_complete.txt.note: **Scans every .py under the app dir and reports each secret-pattern match.**

extra/security_gate_complete.txt.title: Dockerfile hardening checks
extra/security_gate_complete.txt.note: **Fails unpinned base images (:latest or no tag) and containers that run as root.**

extra/security_gate_complete.txt.title: Dependency CVE check
extra/security_gate_complete.txt.note: **Compares each pinned dependency to the CVE db; flags versions below fixed_in.**
